# Binary analysis fixtures

Small PE, ELF, and Mach-O binaries for the triage, debug-symbol, and disassembly tests. All of
them are built from `fixture.c` in this directory, which is original to Hexlora, and contain no
third-party code. They are inspected by the tests and never executed.

| File | What it is | What it exercises |
|---|---|---|
| `fixture-x64.exe` | x86-64 Windows console executable | imports, exports, `.pdata` functions, import hash, capability rules |
| `fixture-x64.pdb` | PDB for `fixture-x64.exe` | PDB identity matching, function names, source lines |
| `fixture-driver.sys` | x86-64 native-subsystem image importing from `ntoskrnl.exe` | kernel driver identification and driver capability rules |
| `fixture-x86_64.elf` | static x86-64 Linux executable with DWARF | ELF symbols, embedded DWARF, x86-64 listings |
| `fixture-aarch64.elf` | static AArch64 Linux executable with DWARF | AArch64 listings |
| `fixture-universal.dylib` | universal Mach-O (x86-64 and arm64) | slices, stubs, the indirect symbol table |

Unlike the IPA fixtures, these are checked in rather than generated by the tests: producing them
needs clang and LLD for three object formats, which ordinary development machines and CI runners
do not all have.

## Rebuilding

`./build.sh` rebuilds everything with clang, `lld-link`, `ld.lld`, `ld64.lld`, `llvm-dlltool`, and
`llvm-lipo` from LLVM 18. The build is reproducible: no timestamps, build IDs, or host paths end
up in the outputs, so rebuilding from an unchanged `fixture.c` leaves the files byte-identical.
Changing `fixture.c` changes addresses and the PDB identity; tests look functions up by name and
read the identity from the files for that reason.
